Bundled datasets

amorem ships the event logs and covariates below, each loadable with data(...). The tables and figures on this page are computed from them when the page is built. The data catalogue documents a wider collection, including datasets whose licences do not allow amorem to redistribute them.

Event logs

object data kind events actors span
classroom_events Classroom (McFarland 2001) face-to-face, minutes 691 20 43.9 minutes
social_evolution_calls Social Evolution calls (Madan et al. 2012) phone calls 439 54 42.1 days
social_evolution_friendship Social Evolution friendship survey tie changes 766 76 40.0 days
radoslaw_email Manufacturing company email (Nurek & Michalski 2020) email 82,927 167 271 days
college_msg CollegeMsg (Panzarasa et al. 2009) instant messages 59,835 1,899 194 days
email_eu_core Email-EU-core, one department (Paranjape et al. 2017) email 12,216 89 802 days
copenhagen_calls Copenhagen Networks Study calls phone calls 3,600 536 28.0 days
copenhagen_sms Copenhagen Networks Study text messages text messages 24,333 568 28.0 days
us_leader_visits US leader-to-leader visits 1945-2019 state visits 3,945 197 27,183 days
football_results Men’s international football since 1872 matches 49,945 337 56,192 days
ucdp_dyads UCDP armed conflict dyads 1946-2025 conflict dyad-years 3,518 704 79.0 years
alien_invasions Alien species first records 1880-2005 species -> region 11,730 3,188 125 years

congress_bills_118 holds hyperevents: each of its 16,213 bills has one sponsor and a set of cosponsors (mean 10.0, largest 331), from 2023-01-03 to 2025-01-03. Actor attributes come in classroom_actors, social_evolution_actors, copenhagen_actors, congress_members_118 and radoslaw_hierarchy.

What each log looks like

For each event log: the network of the actors in its busiest pairs, then when the 30 most active of them are active. The data catalogue adds a close-up of single events and the counting processes of the busiest pairs.

classroom_events

The 20 actors of the busiest pairs, out of 20; events between two of them are 100.0% of all events. Each actor’s three strongest ties are drawn (39 of 73 pairs that ever interacted): wider, darker lines carry more events, larger dots are more active actors, and colours are groups found by modularity (Louvain).

Each row is one of the 20 most active actors of the network, coloured by its group there; a cell is darker the more events (with anyone) the actor took part in during that stretch of time. The grey bars on top count all 691 events.

Who is active

Share of all events in which the most active 10% of actors take part, and the Gini coefficient of actor activity (0 when all actors are equally active):

object events with the top 10% of actors Gini
classroom_events 23.4% 0.29
social_evolution_calls 57.1% 0.68
social_evolution_friendship 27.1% 0.40
radoslaw_email 40.9% 0.62
college_msg 60.2% 0.75
email_eu_core 34.3% 0.53
copenhagen_calls 42.8% 0.59
copenhagen_sms 61.3% 0.73
us_leader_visits 72.0% 0.79
football_results 30.2% 0.54
ucdp_dyads 58.9% 0.70
alien_invasions 62.7% 0.70

Logs with highly concentrated activity are where count statistics carry sender and receiver activity rather than dyadic history; see Analyses of bundled event logs for a comparison with and without a sender frailty.

Global covariates

  • enso_nino34: tree-ring reconstruction of the winter Niño3.4 anomaly, 1301-2005 (see vignette("species-invasion")); oni: the instrumental Oceanic Niño Index since 1950.
  • daily_weather: daily temperature and precipitation at Boston (Social Evolution, 2008), Santa Ana (CollegeMsg, 2004), and Warsaw and Wroclaw (manufacturing email, 2010).
  • public_holidays: public holidays for the same countries and years.

They take one value at a time for every pair, so their effects are estimated with time-shifted sampling (sample_non_events(shift = "exponential")); the email case study does this with the clock.

dist_matrix holds distances between 56 US states and territories, used by the validation experiments.

Time conventions

Event times are days since the first event, except classroom_events (minutes since the start of the class), ucdp_dyads (year) and alien_invasions (years start and stop). Where the source gives clock time, attr(x, "unix_origin") holds the Unix time of time = 0:

format(as.POSIXct(attr(radoslaw_email, "unix_origin"), origin = "1970-01-01",
                  tz = "Europe/Warsaw"), usetz = TRUE)
## [1] "2010-01-02 17:40:10 CET"
format(as.POSIXct(attr(college_msg, "unix_origin"), origin = "1970-01-01",
                  tz = "America/Los_Angeles"), usetz = TRUE)
## [1] "2004-04-15 07:56:01 PDT"
